dedupe_keys.name: gem global seismic hazard map version 2026 1

description: The GEM Global Seismic Hazard Map is a probabilistic seismic hazard map of the whole globe, including the oceans, showing peak ground acceleration with a 10 percent probability of exceedance in 50 years on reference rock (VS30 of 800 m/s). Version 2026.1, published on 23 June 2026 and replacing v2023.1, collates national and regional probabilistic hazard models developed by many institutions with GEM Foundation scientists, all converted to the OpenQuake NRML format and computed with the open-source OpenQuake Engine, with checks against the original results. It is authored by Kendra Johnson, Kirsty Bayliss, Manuela Villani and colleagues at the GEM Foundation, and technical details of the underlying models are documented on hazard.openquake.org. The map is accessible on Zenodo as a free vector zip of about 935 MB under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, so commercial use needs another licence from GEM. Caveats: low-hazard areas may still have damaging earthquakes, values are for rock and ignore local site amplification, and the source models differ in age and method between regions. It supports hazard exposure screening and scenario selection for seismic risk to infrastructure networks across sectors; related records are the OpenQuake Engine, the GEM liquefaction hazard map and ThinkHazard.
